description: Guide a student to find and fix an order type bug in a LEAN momentum strategy where LimitOrder at current price is used instead of MarketOrder, causing most orders to go unfilled in trending markets.

student_openings.beginner_no_finance: My LEAN momentum strategy barely makes any trades even though the signals are firing. I'm placing orders but they don't seem to get filled. What am I doing wrong?
student_openings.intermediate_developer: I have a ROCP-based momentum strategy in LEAN that generates correct signals but the trade count is extremely low. I'm using LimitOrder with the current price. Could the order type be the issue?
student_openings.advanced_quant: My momentum strategy has a severe fill-rate problem — most orders expire unfilled. I'm placing limit orders at the last close price but in a trending market the price gaps away. I need help identifying the correct order execution approach.

ground_truth.expected_outcome: Student replaces LimitOrder(_btc, qty, Securities[_btc].Price) with MarketOrder(_btc, qty) to ensure immediate fills, and understands why limit orders at stale prices fail in trending markets.
required_capabilities: Read the LEAN C# code and identify the order type
Understand why LimitOrder at current price fails in trends
Replace with MarketOrder for guaranteed fills
Verify increased trade count after fix
Compile and run the fixed algorithm
